newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Cargolux 1996 profit down, sees better 1997.
newsitem.headline: Cargolux 1996 profit down, sees better 1997.

text.p: Luxembourg freight carrier Cargolux Airlines International SA said on Wednesday that higher fuel prices and lower yields pushed down 1996 earnings but that 1997 results looked more promising.

Cargolux' 1996 net profit fell to $7.33 million from $15.31 million in the year-earlier period. Freight carried rose to 233,914, a new record, from 217,057 tonnes. Revenues rose to $396.66 million from $389.07 million.
Cargolux, Europe's seventh-largest freight carrier, said, however, business improved in the last quarter of 1996 and the trend had continued into this year.
"The first months of 1997 show encouraging business results...The company is cautiously optimistic that 1997 will again bring satisfying results," the company said in a statement.

Cargolux noted the planned addition to its fleet of two new Boeing 747-400 aircraft in August and November would have a positive impact on its performance. The company presently operates four 747-200 and three 747-400 aircraft.
Cargolux is 30.50 percent held by Luxembourg airline Luxair. German airline Lufthansa owns 24.50 percent and the remainder is held by numerous Luxembourg financial institutions and holding companies.
